correctness.rationale: For FARL-to-monadic, Wang--Shi--Wang's derived implication, join, fixed-point, and adjunction identities give the nontrivial monadic axioms, while the Gödel product is idempotent so the square/product axiom becomes automatic. Conversely, the standard monadic Gödel structure theorem identifies the common image \(F=\exists G=\forall G\) as a Gödel subalgebra and makes \(\forall\) and \(\exists\) the lower and upper approximations to \(F\); these rounding formulas give the Galois adjunction and the three Frobenius laws. On a finite chain every endpoint-containing subset is a Gödel subalgebra, and the rounding pair is unique, yielding exactly \(2^{n-2}\) expansions. The inspected verifier exhaustively compares both axiom systems on small chains and on the four-element product algebra as corroboration.

originality.rationale: Wang--Shi--Wang introduce FARL and explicitly prove that FARL and monadic residuated lattices are incomparable in general, but their inspected full text contains no Gödel specialization. The older monadic-Gödel paper gives the common-image rounding structure but predates FARL. Combining these strands to prove exact coincidence on all Gödel algebras therefore supplies a genuine boundary theorem rather than a special case already stated by either source.

value.rationale: The defining FARL paper emphasizes that its new class and monadic residuated lattices are incomparable. Identifying a canonical and widely studied idempotent subclass where they coincide exactly, together with a complete finite-chain normal form, is a natural structural boundary result rather than an arbitrary specialization.

final_claim: On every Gödel algebra, Frobenius-adjoint residuated-lattice expansions coincide exactly with monadic Gödel expansions under \(f=\forall\) and \(g=\exists\); on the \(n\)-element Gödel chain the common expansions are exactly the lower/upper rounding pairs to endpoint-containing subchains, so their number is \(2^{n-2}\).
limitations: The coincidence is specific to the Gödel setting; it is false for general residuated lattices.
The exact power-of-two count is only for finite chains, not arbitrary finite Gödel algebras.
